object.title: Kinser-minus separation conjecture
object.statement:
For an integer $n>5$, let ${\mathrm{Kin}(n)}^-$ denote the matroid referred to in the source as ${\mathrm{Kin}(n)}^-$. Let $\mathcal{K}_n$ be the class of matroids satisfying the $n$-th Kinser inequality, and let $\mathcal{K}_n^*$ be its dual class. **Kinser-minus separation conjecture.**

$$
{\mathrm{Kin}(n)}^-\in\mathcal{K}_n^* - \mathcal{K}_n.
$$

The source presents this as a strengthening of the conjecture that $\mathcal{K}_n$ is not dual closed, motivated by the difficulty of the fifth case. The notation ${\mathrm{Kin}(n)}^-$ is not defined in the supplied context.
object.source_name: Amanda Cameron, “Kinser inequalities and related matroids”, arXiv:1401.0500 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0500

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

object.title: Infinite Kinser class self-duality conjecture
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{K}_\infty$ denote the class obtained from the hierarchy of Kinser classes, and let $\mathcal{K}_\infty^*$ denote its dual class. **Infinite Kinser class self-duality conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{K}_\infty^*=\mathcal{K}_\infty.
$$

The source states that this conjecture would follow from the preceding dual-containment conjecture. It therefore remains open unless that preceding conjecture is proved.

object.title: Finiteness conjecture for connected 3-CS-transitive 2-level posets
object.statement:
Let $M$ be a connected 3-$CS$-transitive 2-level poset. Let $M^D$ be its dual poset, and let $I$ be an interval of $M^D$. Suppose that

$$
I \not\cong C_2 \quad\text{and}\quad I \not\cong C_3.
$$

**Finiteness conjecture.** The poset $M$ is finite if and only if the interval $I$ is finite.

The preceding result establishes the converse direction under the same hypotheses, while the forward direction is conjectured here. The exclusions of $C_2$ and $C_3$ are necessary for the preceding result, but the source gives no resolution of this conjecture.
object.source_name: Robert D. Gray and John K. Truss, “Countable locally 2-arc-transitive bipartite graphs”, arXiv:1401.2681 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.2681

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

object.title: List rankability of trees with more leaves than internal vertices
object.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree with $p$ internal vertices and $q$ leaves, and let $\rho _{\ell}(T)$ denote its list-ranking number. **Tree list-ranking conjecture.** If $p<q$, then

$$
\rho _{\ell}(T)=q.
$$

This would give equality in the general lower bound supplied by a subtree with many leaves, beyond the class of trees established by the paper's third main theorem. The conjecture is presented as an apparent strengthening of that theorem, and no resolution is supplied here.

object.title: The nonzero-variety dot-product conjecture
object.statement:
Let $\mathbb F_q$ be a finite field, let $Q\in\mathbb F_q[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$, and define the variety

$$
V=\{x\in\mathbb F_q^d:Q(x)=0\}.
$$

Assume that $(0,\ldots,0)\notin V$. For $E\subset V$ and $F\subset\mathbb F_q^d$, let

$$
\Pi(E,F)=\{x\cdot y:x\in E,y\in F\}.
$$

**Nonzero-variety dot-product conjecture.** If $|E||F|\gg_C q^d$, then

$$
|\Pi(E,F)|\gg_c q.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the corresponding theorem for spheres and translated paraboloids, but no resolution is given in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Doowon Koh and Youngjin Pi, “Size of dot product sets determined by pairs of subsets of vector spaces over finite fields”, arXiv:1401.6992 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.6992

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

object.title: Weighted covering conjecture for d-interval hypergraphs
object.statement:
Let $H$ be a hypergraph of $d$-intervals, let $\tau_w(H)$ be its weighted covering number, and let $\nu_w(H)$ be its weighted matching number. **Weighted covering conjecture.** One should have

$$
\tau_w(H) \le d^2\nu_w(H).
$$
 This bound would improve the proved general estimate $\tau_w(H)\le 2d^2\nu_w(H)$ and would follow in the separated case from the weighted fractional covering conjecture. Its validity in the general case remains open.
object.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Tomas Kaiser and Shira Zerbib, “Fractional covers and matchings in families of weighted d-intervals”, arXiv:1402.2064 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.2064

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2014). “An open question in is whether $\tau^*<3$ for intersecting families of (non-separated) 2-intervals.”

object.title: Laplacian Nordhaus–Gaddum product equality characterization conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices, let $\overline G$ be its complement, and let $K_1$ denote the one-vertex complete graph. The **join** of graphs is denoted by $\vee$. **Laplacian product conjecture.**

$$
\mu_1(G)\mu_1(\overline G)\leq n(n-1),
$$

and equality holds if and only if $G$ or $\overline G$ is isomorphic to $K_1\vee H$ for a disconnected graph $H$ of order $n-1$. The inequality is proved in the source for bipartite graphs, while the general assertion and its equality characterization are left open.
object.source_name: F. Ashraf and B. Tayfeh-Rezaie, “Nordhaus–Gaddum type inequalities for Laplacian and signless Laplacian eigenvalues”, arXiv:1402.2995 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.2995

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2014).

object.title: The lcm-maximal piece conjecture for coefficient periods
object.statement:
For a piece $\mathbb P$ with move set $\mathbf{M}$, write

$$
\hat d_r:=\max(|c_r|,|d_r|).
$$

For a positive integer $\lambda$, let $\mathbb P^{\operatorname{lcm}}_\lambda$ be the lcm-maximal piece whose move set consists of all moves $(c,d)$ satisfying $\hat d\mid\lambda$. **Lcm-maximal piece conjecture.** Among all pieces satisfying

$$
\operatorname{lcm}\{\hat d_r:m_r\in\mathbf{M}\}=\lambda,
$$

$\mathbb P^{\operatorname{lcm}}_\lambda$ maximizes the period of every coefficient $\gamma_i$, for fixed $q$.

This conjecture is motivated by the proposed period bounds for $\gamma_3$ and $\gamma_4$; the paper gives no proof or general resolution.
object.source_name: Seth Chaiken, Christopher R. H. Hanusa and Thomas Zaslavsky, “A q-Queens Problem. II. The Square Board”, arXiv:1402.4880 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.4880

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

object.title: The dimension-reduction conjecture for generalized Fibonacci cubes
object.statement:
Let $f$ and $f'$ be binary strings, and let $Q_d(f)$ be the generalized Fibonacci cube of dimension $d$ defined by forbidding $f$. The notation $Q_d(f)\cong Q_d(f')$ means that these graphs are isomorphic.

**Dimension-reduction conjecture.** If

$$
f,f'\text{ are binary strings and }Q_d(f)\cong Q_d(f'),
$$

then

$$
Q_{d-1}(f)\cong Q_{d-1}(f').
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the paper's extremal isomorphism theorem, which gives explicit non-trivial isomorphisms in a range of dimensions; it asks whether every such isomorphism persists after reducing the dimension by one.
object.source_name: Jernej Azarija, Sandi Klavžar, Jaehun Lee, Jay Pantone and Yoomi Rho, “On Isomorphism Classes of Generalized Fibonacci Cubes”, arXiv:1402.6377 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.6377

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

object.title: Loehr–Warrington rational $q$-Catalan partition formula conjecture
object.statement:
Fix $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$ with $\gcd(a,b)=1$. Let $\mathrm{D}(a,b)$ be the set of partitions whose diagrams fit in the triangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(0,a)$, and $(b,a)$. For a cell $c$, let $\mathsf{arm}(c)$ and $\mathsf{leg}(c)$ denote its arm and leg, and let $h^+_{b,a}(\mu)$ count cells satisfying $-a<a\mathsf{arm}(c)-b\mathsf{leg}(c)\leq b$. **Rational $q$-Catalan formula conjecture.**

$$
\mathsf{Cat}_{a,b}(q)=\sum_{\mu\in\mathrm{D}(a,b)}q^{|\mu|+h^+_{b,a}(\mu)}.
$$

This proposes a partition-statistic interpretation of the rational $q$-Catalan number; the supplied text does not give a proof or resolution.
object.source_name: Drew Armstrong, Nicholas A. Loehr and Gregory S. Warrington, “Rational parking functions and Catalan numbers”, arXiv:1403.1845 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.1845

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2014). “The Shuffle Conjecture (which is still open) gives such a precise description.”

object.title: The conjecture that planar graphs are (4,2)-choosable
object.statement: A **$(k,s)$-list assignment** $L$ assigns a list $L(v)$ of $k$ colors to each vertex of a graph, with $|L(u)\cap L(v)|\leq s$ whenever $uv$ is an edge. A graph is **$(k,s)$-choosable** if every such list assignment admits a proper coloring choosing a color from each vertex's list. **Planar $(4,2)$-choosability conjecture.** If $G$ is a planar graph, then $G$ is $(4,2)$-choosable. The paper states that it is not known whether all planar graphs have this property; this is the motivating open question for its study of 4-choosability with separation.
object.source_name: Zhanar Berikkyzy, Christopher Cox, Michael Dairyko, Kirsten Hogenson, Mohit Kumbhat, Bernard Lidický, Kacy Messerschmidt, Kevin Moss, Kathleen Nowak, Kevin F. Palmowski and Derrick Stolee, “(4,2)-choosability of planar graphs with forbidden structures”, arXiv:1512.03787 (2015).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03787

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2015).

object.title: The radial subtiling conjecture for monohedral disk tilings
object.statement:
A **monohedral disk tiling** is a tiling of the disk by congruent tiles. A tiling is **radially generated** when it is constructed by the radial generation described in the paper, and a **subtiling** is a tiling obtained by subdividing tiles in the specified manner.

**Radial subtiling conjecture.** Any monohedral tiling of the disk is a subtiling of a radially generated tiling.

The conjecture would reduce the classification of all monohedral disk tilings to radially generated tilings and their allowed subtilings. The paper classifies the radially generated tilings and several families of their subtilings, but does not establish that every monohedral disk tiling arises this way.
object.source_name: Joel Haddley and Stephen Worsley, “Infinite families of monohedral disk tilings”, arXiv:1512.03794 (2016).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03794

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2015).

object.title: The complete classification conjecture for monohedral disk tilings
object.statement:
A **monohedral disk tiling** is a tiling of the disk by congruent tiles. The paper's constructions include radially generated tilings and the subtilings of wedge tilings described in the preceding conjectures.

**Complete classification conjecture.** The full classification of monohedral disk tilings is present in this paper.

The authors explain that their results classify the constructed families and that, together with the radial subtiling conjecture, the preceding subtiling classification would imply this final conjecture. The supplied text presents it as a remaining conjecture rather than as an established theorem.

object.title: The complete-list conjecture for Ulrich partition types
object.statement:
Let $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ be the type of an Ulrich partition, and call two types symmetric when they are identified by the symmetry used in the paper. Here $n$ is a positive integer, and each $k_i$ has the form

$$
k_i=\frac{4^{m_i+1}-1}{3}
$$

for some $m_i\geq0$. **Complete-list conjecture.** Up to symmetry, the type $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ is one of

$$
(1,n,1),\quad (1,n,2),\quad (2,2n,2),\quad (2,2,3),\quad (2,1,k_1),\quad (1,2,k_1),\quad (1,2,k_1+k_2).
$$

The conjecture proposes that the examples obtained in the paper exhaust all Ulrich partition types for two-step flag varieties. The paper gives partial classifications and states that the classification remains incomplete, so the conjecture is open.
object.source_name: Izzet Coskun, Laura Costa, Jack Huizenga, Rosa Maria Miró-Roig and Matthew Woolf, “Ulrich Schur bundles on flag varieties”, arXiv:1512.06193 (2015).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.06193

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2015).

object.title: Cherlin's almost simple binary primitive group conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ be an almost simple primitive permutation group acting on a set $\Omega$, and suppose that its permutation action is **binary**. **Cherlin's almost simple conjecture.** Then

$$
G=\operatorname{Sym}(\Omega).
$$

This statement is presented as sufficient for proving Cherlin's classification conjecture and is reduced from the original conjecture using work of Cherlin and Wiscons. The supplied context does not establish whether this almost simple statement is proved in full, so its status is recorded as open.
object.source_name: Nick Gill, Francesca Dalla Volta and Pablo Spiga, “Cherlin's conjecture for sporadic simple groups”, arXiv:1705.05150 (2018).
object.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.05150

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2017).

object.title: Strong rainbow connection number bound by forest number
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. Write $\operatorname{src}(G)$ for its strong rainbow connection number and $\operatorname{f}(G)$ for its forest number.

**Strong rainbow connection conjecture.** A connected graph $G$ has

$$
\operatorname{src}(G) \leq \operatorname{f}(G)-1.
$$

The source presents this as a stronger version of the preceding rainbow connection conjecture, attributed to Lauri and discovered using the automated conjecture-making software GraPHedron. Its status remains open in the supplied text.

object.title: Vanishing conjecture for homology below virtual cohomological dimension
object.statement: Let $\Gamma_{n,s}$ be the graph automorphism group with parameters $n$ and $s$, and let $2n+s-3$ be its virtual cohomological dimension. **Below-vcd vanishing conjecture.** All classes in $H_k(\Gamma_{n,s})$ for $0<k<2n+s-3$ vanish after a single stabilization with respect to $n$. This is presented as a consequence of the assembly-generation and stabilization-vanishing conjectures, so it remains open to the extent that those conjectures are unresolved.

This is presented as a consequence of the assembly-generation and stabilization-vanishing conjectures, so it remains open to the extent that those conjectures are unresolved."

object.title: The incorrect-path splitting conjecture for polar-code list decoding
object.statement:
Let $u_i$ be an unfrozen bit in a polar code, and consider any incorrect decoding path that survives at $u_i$. Under the Gaussian approximation, the path may continue through subsequent unfrozen bits $u_{i+1},\ldots,u_N$.

**Incorrect-path splitting conjecture.** Under the Gaussian approximation, for any incorrect path that survives at some unfrozen bit $u_i$, it will split at some stage within $\{i+1,i+2,\ldots,N\}$ with high probability.

This conjecture concerns the behavior of incorrect paths in successive-cancellation list decoding. Together with the preceding conjecture about the correct path, it is intended to describe how splitting and pruning affect path survival, but the source provides empirical evidence rather than a proof.
object.source_name: Zhaoyang Zhang, Liang Zhang, Xianbin Wang, Caijun Zhong and H. Vincent Poor, “A Split-Reduced Successive Cancellation List Decoder for Polar Codes”, arXiv:1511.02150 (2015).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.02150

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2015).

object.title: Automorphism-group conjecture for rectangular-combination designs
object.statement:
Let $\widetilde{\mathscr{D}}$ be a design and let ${\mathscr{D}}(\widetilde{\mathscr{D}},(e_1,e_2))$ denote the design obtained from it by the rectangular combination construction, with positive integers $e_1,e_2$. **Automorphism-group conjecture.** If $e_1\geq 3$, then

$$
\operatorname{Aut}({\mathscr{D}}(\widetilde{\mathscr{D}},(e_1,e_2)))=\operatorname{Aut}(\widetilde{\mathscr{D}})\wr(S_{e_1}\times S_{e_2}).
$$

This conjecture proposes that the exceptional enlargement of the automorphism group observed when $e_1=2$ does not occur for $e_1\geq 3$; the claim remains open in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Carmen Amarra, Alice Devillers and Cheryl E. Praeger, “Recursive constructions for block-transitive, poset-imprimitive two-designs”, arXiv:2607.03029 (2026).
object.references:
**11 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2603.07707](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.07707), [arXiv:2602.15264](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.15264), [arXiv:2504.05721](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05721), [arXiv:2408.06283](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.06283), [arXiv:2407.19745](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.19745), [arXiv:2306.10744](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.10744), [arXiv:1907.06008](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.06008), [arXiv:1810.12855](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.12855), [arXiv:1704.08474](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.08474), [arXiv:1508.07279](https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.07279).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03029

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).
